pick.counterargument: It is an expensive stock: 55.6× trailing earnings and a 3.4% free cash flow yield, so the growth is already in the price and one weak quarter would cost a lot. growth decelerated against the previous quarter, so the trend in the numbers is already turning.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +53.0%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $72.56 on the decision date.
risks: The share count is from 2026-09-30, 50 days older than the price, so the market capitalisation carries that staleness.
The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-09-30, 50 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-11-19.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2026-02-10) plus 364 days

pick.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
pick.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.title: Irène Sapir escaped the Holocaust. Far-right councilors opposed naming a school after her.
stories.excerpt: A school in Bergerac, southwestern France, has been renamed after the 89-year-old local Communist figure who escaped deportation during the 1942 Vél d'Hiv roundup and has since kept the memory alive. stories.title: New draft deal aims to avert collapse of talks at COP31 climate summit
stories.excerpt: The UN COP31 meeting in Turkey enters a second day of overtime as countries struggle to reach an agreement.
stories.lead:
Efforts to avert the collapse of talks at the UN COP31 summit have faced further delays on the second day of overtime, as countries struggle to reach a new global climate deal.

A new draft agreement was published in the early hours of Sunday which the Turkey and Australia co-hosts hoped would bridge the divide between nations.

Although it still includes no specific reference to "transitioning away from fossil fuels" - an omission in the previous draft that sparked threats of walkouts - it does acknowledge a previous commitment made by countries to do just that three years ago.

stories.title: Trump orders federal contractors to check with White House before responding to Congress
stories.excerpt: President Trump is directing federal contractors to consult the White House about inquiries from Congress and to withhold any communications that his administration considers privileged.
stories.lead:
NEW YORK (AP) — President Donald Trump is directing federal contractors and subcontractors to consult with his administration about inquiries they receive from Congress and to withhold any communications that the White House considers privileged, according to a new executive order.

The companies must also coordinate with the White House and U.S. agencies on "appropriate responses" to any such requests, the order issued late Friday says. If they fail to comply, the White House warns their contracts could be terminated and their future work with the federal government suspended.

stories.title: FBI reportedly investigating apparent hack of its criminal database
stories.excerpt: The National Crime Information Center database is used by federal and local law enforcement to share information.
stories.lead:
The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its criminal information database, US media reports, citing two people briefed on the issue.

It would not be the first time hackers have targeted the FBI, the domestic intelligence and security service of the US. The agency did not respond to the BBC's request for comment.

stories.title: Google employees protest AI in schools policy

stories.lead: Parents and educators want Google to provide an AI-free version of the search engine for students. Now some Google employees are joining in the push to provide AI-free access to students. NPR education reporter Sequoia Carrillo is following the story. She joins us now. Hey, Sequoia.

stories.title: Mexican drug lord on FBI's 10 most wanted list arrested in shoot-out
stories.excerpt: Fausto Isidro "Chapo Idisro" Meza Flores, who is accused of drug trafficking and torture, is detained after gun fight with authorities.
stories.lead:
A Mexican drug lord who was on the FBI's 10 most wanted list has been arrested following a shoot-out with Mexican authorities.

Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza Flores and seven others were detained by Mexican special forces in Guasave, Sinaloa on Friday, Mexico's defence secretariat said.

Seven suspects were killed in the operation, as were four members of the Mexican army who were travelling to reinforce security in Guasave, the secretariat added.

stories.title: MP criticises Guernsey and Jersey company ownership register plans
stories.excerpt: Sir Andrew Mitchell says access should be easier for people tackling financial crime.
stories.lead:
Plans to improve transparency over company ownership in Guernsey and Jersey have come under criticism from a Westminster MP, who says they "do not go nearly far enough".

The comments come after Guernsey, external and Jersey, external set out plans to allow approved applicants access to information about who owns or controls companies when investigating suspected financial crime.

Sir Andrew Mitchell, who has campaigned for greater scrutiny of company ownership, said there were "immediate indications" the proposals would fall short.

stories.title: Italian jeweller and businessman Paolo Bulgari dies aged 89
stories.excerpt: In a statement to Italian media, his family remember him as "the greatest jeweller of our time".
stories.lead:
Italian jeweller Paolo Bulgari, who helped turn his family's business into a global luxury brand, has died in Rome aged age 89.

His family announced the news, remembering him as "the greatest jeweller of our time", according to Italian media.

Paolo Bulgari was Chairman of the Bvlgari Group since 1984 and its jewellery pieces have adorned Hollywood stars and royalty including Diana, Princess of Wales.

stories.title: Water Polo Advances to MAWPC Championship Game
stories.excerpt: Water polo defeats Mount St. Mary's to advance to MAWPC championship game.
stories.lead:
Lewisburg, Pa. – The Fordham men's water polo squad took one step closer to its sixth straight MAWPC, defeating Mount St. Mary's today, 17-7, at Bucknell's Kinney Natatorium to advance to the championship game. The Rams will face Navy for the MAWPC title on Sunday at Noon.

With the win, Fordham improves to 24-3 on the season while Mount St. Mary's falls to 12-17.

Junior Andras Toth led the Rams with three goals and four assists while sophomore Alessandro Salipante scored twice and had three assists.
